chunk_findings.detail: The document is written (`target.write_text`) and committed (`W.commit(wt, ...)`) into the task's worktree *before* any chore authorisation is checked, so a call that the function itself reports as refused has already mutated repository state. Concrete input: a project whose approved chore globs (`[chore].globs`) do not cover `docs/ddflow/decisions`, run `ddflow decide ST-x --decision-id D-y` (task globs include the doc path, D-y is live, ST-x is leased). Execution reaches `made = W.commit(...)`, which creates the commit `decision D-y: <title>` on the item's branch, and only then does `approved = CO.standing(st, cfg)` fail and return `O.refused(..., "a person runs ddflow chore approve")`. The operator/agent sees a refusal whose message says "the task stays open", but the unapproved decision document is now committed to the branch (and present in the working tree). Any later path that consumes that branch — an explicit `ddflow merge ST-x`, an automated merge, or a retry whose authorisation decision is computed from the pre-write state (`st` was loaded by `_load` before `write_text`, and `CO.standing` is handed no representation of `rel`) — can therefore land the exact file the check exists to gate, without the approval ever having covered it. Moving the `CO.standing` check before the write/commit (or undoing the commit on refusal) is needed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/decide.py:decide (the `CO.standing(st, cfg)` check placed after `W.commit`)

chunk_findings.detail: The change matches `DECIDE_TAGS` against the item's **raw** tag list, while the sibling hunk in the same diff (`ddflow/services/chore.py:81`) deliberately normalizes before matching the very same constant (`tags = {t.strip().lower() for t in it.tags}`; the pre-existing line it replaces also did `t.strip().lower()`). When a record carries the tag in any non-canonical form — e.g. `tags: [Decide]`, or a trailing space from an inline list such as `tags: [task, decide ]` — `DECIDE_TAGS & {"Decide"}` is the empty set, so the new guard is false and control falls through to the ancestor loop, re-inheriting the phase's needs. The operator then still gets "phase P-harness-adapters has 8 open tasks inherited from P-agent-parity" and cannot claim the decide task, which is precisely the failure this change exists to remove. Note the same input *is* accepted as a decide chore one file over (`{TAG} | DECIDE_TAGS` intersects after `.strip().lower()`), so the two call sites of the same constant disagree: a task can simultaneously be "a decide task that writes only a document" for reviewer exemption and "still gate-blocked" for claimability. Either both sites must normalize identically, or the tag matching must be documented as case/whitespace-sensitive and the tags canonicalized upstream.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/schedule.py:286 (`DECIDE_TAGS & set(it.tags)`)

chunk_findings.detail: This still holds: the diff part I can see does not normalize the tag list, and the finding is untriaged. chunk_findings.detail: The reorder does move the standing check ahead of `target.write_text`/`W.commit`, so the literal "mutation happens before the check reports refusal" complaint is gone. But the check still does not answer the scenario it was raised for, because `CO.standing(st, cfg)` is given no path: it can only report whether *some* standing chore approval exists, never whether that approval's `[chore].globs` actually cover the document about to be committed. The function even asserts the opposite in its own refusal text ("a decision document lands under the approved chore list ([chore].globs)"), but nothing verifies `rel` against `cfg.chore.globs` — only against the task's own `it.globs`. Concrete input: a project with `[chore].globs = ["src/**"]`, a live standing approval, and a leased decide task whose globs include `docs/ddflow/decisions/**`; running `ddflow decide ST-x --decision-id D-y` takes the `approved.ok` branch, writes `docs/ddflow/decisions/<slug>.md`, and commits it under the standing-approval note (`standing approval …@<digest>`), i.e. a file outside the approved chore list is committed as a chore with no authorization covering it. The fix needs a coverage test such as `inside(rel, g) for g in cfg.chore.globs` (or an equivalent path passed into `CO.standing`) before the write, not just an earlier ordering of the path-agnostic call.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/decide.py:decide (`approved = CO.standing(st, cfg)`)

chunk_findings.detail: `render=lambda out, a: out.data.get("text") or out.reason` is the only thing that turns a successful run into user-visible output, but the command's declared payload `("item", "decision", "path", "sha", "skipped_gates", "stage")` does not contain `"text"`. The outcome data for a declared command is assembled from its payload keys, so `out.data.get("text")` is always `None` and the renderer always falls through to `out.reason`. Given a live record `D-y` and a leased decide task `ST-x`, `ddflow decide ST-x --decision-id D-y` performs the write/commit/complete correctly but prints the refusal-style `reason` (typically an empty string on success) instead of the "written docs/ddflow/decisions/…, closed ST-x" message the renderer was written to show; the command silently appears to produce nothing. Either `"text"` belongs in `PAYLOAD`, or the renderer must not read a key the payload deliberately excludes.

chunk_findings.detail: The new probe that is supposed to close prior finding 2 only exercises the *case* half of it: `_queue(proj, "Decide")` inserts the single tag `Decide` (no padding), and the assertion `inherited_deps(...) == []` then only proves that a lower-casing comparison (or a CLI that already lower-cases) works. It cannot distinguish a fix that normalises with `t.strip().lower()` from a minimal fix that only does `t.lower()`, because nothing in the test ever produces a tag with surrounding whitespace. Prior finding 2's concrete input was a raw record, e.g. `tags: [task, decide ]`, where the item's raw tag set is `{"decide "}`; with the sibling read path in the same change doing `tags = {t.strip().lower() for t in it.tags}` the schedule side must strip as well, and a padded tag fed straight from a record (not through `task add --tags`, which is the only route this test uses) would still yield `DECIDE_TAGS & {"decide "} == set()` and make the decide task inherit `P-next -> P-gate` again. The probe therefore does not answer the padding scenario of the finding, and the test name asserting padding coverage is misleading: writing the probe with `--tags "Decide "` (argv preserves the trailing space) or by appending the tag to the record directly would have covered it.

chunk_findings.detail: The verb's contract (docstring lines 5–6: "records the remaining gates skipped (the record is the operator's own words), merges and completes") is not what the loop implements. The loop only records a skip for gates that also appear in `cfg.chore.skip_gates`; every other gate left in `G.status(...).pipeline` (line 139) is neither satisfied nor skipped, so `merge_item` (line 148) fails with an unsatisfied-gate error and `_fail("merge", ...)` returns. Concretely, the scenario that motivated the verb — a decide task whose pipeline still carries an inherited/phase gate that is not in `[chore].skip_gates`, e.g. the filing's "phase P-harness-adapters has 8 open tasks inherited from P-agent-parity" — writes and commits the document on the worktree branch (lines 129–134) but then dies at merge, leaving the task open and the document unlanded, i.e. the same "abandoned" outcome the change exists to eliminate. Either the loop must record skips for all non-`merge` gates in the decide task's pipeline, or the docstring/promise ("nothing is abandoned") is false; as written, a decide task is only decidable when every remaining gate happens to be chore-skippable.
chunk_findings.location: ddflow/api/decide.py:142 (`for gate in pipeline: if gate == "merge" or gate not in cfg.chore.skip_gates: continue`)

chunk_findings.detail: The exemption is keyed only on `it.tags` (`is_decide(it.tags)`), never on `it.kind`, even though the change's own rule is "inherited phase gates never apply to a task tagged decide/kind decision". `is_decide` receives only the tag list, so an item recorded as `kind: decision` (or any kind other than the tagged form) with no `decide`/`decision` entry in `tags` makes `is_decide` return False; the branch is not taken, and the code goes on to build `mine` and append every open descendant of the ancestor phases to `pairs`. Claiming such an item therefore still fails with exactly the error the change exists to remove ("phase P-harness-adapters has 8 open tasks inherited from P-agent-parity"), and `ddflow decide <id> --decision-id D-x` is the only way left to close it — i.e. the reported defect ("I abandoned the task 'done as a decision'") survives for the kind-based form of decide task. The companion edit in `chore.py` shows the model treats `kind` and `tags` as independent (`it.kind != "task"` short-circuits before the tag test), and it also returns `(None, "")` for such an item, so the same gap appears in both halves: nothing in the change consults the kind at all. Either `is_decide` needs the item (or a separate `it.kind == "decision"` test) in `schedule.py`, or the intent's "kind decision" case is silently unsupported.

Claiming such an item therefore still fails with exactly the error the change exists to remove ("phase P-harness-adapters has 8 open tasks inherited from P-agent-parity"), and `ddflow decide <id> --decision-id D-x` is the only way left to close it — i.e. the reported defect ("I abandoned the task 'done as a decision'") survives for the kind-based form of decide task. The companion edit in `chore.py` shows the model treats `kind` and `tags` as independent (`it.kind != "task"` short-circuits before the tag test), and it also returns `(None, "")` for such an item, so the same gap appears in both halves: nothing in the change consults the kind at all. Either `is_decide` needs the item (or a separate `it.kind == "decision"` test) in `schedule.py`, or the intent's "kind decision" case is silently unsupported.
